We have not tried weighted pool4 softmax, median pool4, trimmed_mean pool4. Also dba pool4. Let's pick median pool4 as robust.

attempts.rationale: Test a robust weighted combination using inverse error to exploit strong seasonality and unstable ranking.
Test a robust median combination to see if reducing influence of outlier models improves SMAPE, given unstable ranking and correlated groups.
Trying a simple mean combination to see if the robust median advantage is specific or if a plain average can beat it given the strong seasonality and stable trend.
Try a per-horizon weighted combination with softmax_neg_error to see if a different weighting scheme improves over inverse_error while still robust to unstable ranking.
Test a per‑horizon best‑model weighted combination to see if switching models across horizons improves SMAPE, given the unstable ranking and strong seasonality.
use pool4 with inverse_error weights to leverage diversity and reduce correlated error
The series has strong seasonality and unstable rankings; a trimmed mean may reduce influence of correlated outliers while keeping more models.
The series shows unstable ranking and strong correlation groups; a robust DBA that can handle outliers may improve over trimmed mean.

test a weighted combination that focuses on the diverse pool4 but uses softmax_neg_error to give more weight to better models while still allowing some diversity (different from previous weighted on pool_full).
The series shows unstable ranking and strong correlated groups; a per‑horizon top‑k mean may capture horizon‑specific strengths.

decision.justification: Selected 'trimmed_mean' (an agent proposal) as the best of 12 backtested attempts, score 0.8602. Series context: trend strength 0.9992 and seasonal strength 1.0; model ranking is unstable across windows (Kendall tau -0.068); 4 of 19 models carry independent error; relative error spread across the pool is 1.435.
